newsitem.title: USA: USDA accepts 16.1 Mln acres for CRP -- Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA accepts 16.1 Mln acres for CRP -- Glickman.

text.p: The Agriculture Department has accepted 16.1 million acres of U.S. farmland for entry into the Conservation Reserve this fall, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday.
During a news conference, Glickman said "16.1 million acres was the common sense answer" to balancing cost of the program and gaining environmental benefits.
Farmers will be notified next week if their bid was accepted.
"We will have another signup this fall," Glickman said.
He said 21.1 million acres were expiring this fall. Of that, 11.7 million acres were re-enrolled. Some 9.5 million acres would return to production and 4.4 new acres were accepted for CRP.
There was no major change in regional enrollments. The Plains and Midwest dominant enrollment.
